parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct; no trans-specific offence, facility ban or documented police targeting of trans people. Extrapolating from structural signals in a thin dossier: no presentation laws, no recorded enforcement or relief, and the country shows a protective external posture (UN LGBTI core group, 2025 regional declaration) and a tolerant society (80%+ acceptance of homosexual neighbours, active Pride, free registration of LGBTI organisations). The 2010 report noting societal discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity is dated, and the only trans-specific harm is the activist's undated two physical attacks and verbal abuse — a thin, dated record that cannot be read as either a pattern or its absence. Friction is likely: no legal gender recognition precedent, no gender-identity protection in law, and all tolerance data is LGB-framed, so trans-specific attitudes are unknown. Open questions (custody placement, border document practice, ward rules) are unresolved rather than exposures, and the resident-facing LGR gap is not visitor-facing. This sits at the 0.65 tier: no organised targeting or universal exclusion, but real friction and uncertainty rather than documented operating protections.
